organizations.csv: Key quality: acct_num is blank on 13 rows and duplicated on 18 rows (999 distinct over 1030 rows). Since organization_id must be unique and every contact/subscription/activity references it, the engineer must resolve blanks and duplicates at validation before load; no exact duplicate rows exist, so the duplicate account numbers carry differing content and would raise 409 conflicts if sent twice.

company_name shows 45 normalized duplicates and 11 case-variant groups, which suggests the same legal entity appears under more than one acct_num. Worth a de-duplication pass before load, separately from the key duplicates above.

Required-field gaps: organization.lifecycle_status is required but company_status is blank on 44 rows (4.3%), and organization.billing_country is required but country is blank on 59 rows (5.7%). Defaults for these blanks are a validation-step decision.

Rule 2 (dormant -> Inactive) interacts with target cross-record rule 'an inactive or churned organization cannot hold a trial or active subscription'. Flipping dormant accounts to inactive will invalidate any still-active subscription rows for those accounts in the subscription dataset; the two datasets need to be reconciled before load.

Customer rule 4 (Strategic accounts always carry Enterprise) and rules 7-12 apply to the subscription dataset, not to this file; the only effect here is that customer_tier = Strategic must be preserved so the subscription load can honour rule 4.

Dates are dirty in both date columns: only ~15% are ISO, six formats are mixed, and there are 4 future created_on values and 5 future last_activity_date values (up to 2027-09-03). Future dates will distort the rule 2 dormancy calculation and should be reviewed at validation.

This file supplies only an email for the primary contact; contact.first_name and contact.last_name are required by the catalog but are not present in organizations.csv. They must come from the CRM contact dataset, or the contacts created from primary_contact_email will fail validation.

Assumption: created_on (CRM record creation) is used as organization.customer_since because it is the only date on the organization entity; for Prospect accounts this means customer_since predates any actual customer relationship.
contacts.csv: Rule 14 is satisfied by construction: no contact is filtered out on opt_out. If Apex later needs the 214 opt-out flags preserved in Meridian, there is no target field for them on contact — that would need a platform change or a side table, not a mapping change.
22 rows (1.0%) have a blank `acct_num`. contact.organization_id is required and must reference an existing organization, so those contacts cannot load as-is; flag at validation.

Rule 1 says the account row's `primary_contact_email` is authoritative when no contact is flagged primary, but contacts.csv contains no such column — it must come from the accounts dataset and be joined on acct_num. Also, 459+199+165+119 = 942 rows evaluate to is_primary = true against 1046 distinct accounts, so some accounts will have several primaries and some none; the 'at most one primary per organization' rule must be enforced at validation, using the account's primary_contact_email as the tie-breaker.

`contact_mail` has 66 normalized duplicates and 33 case-variant groups; after lower-casing, some of these may collide within the same organization, which violates 'email is unique within an organization'. Resolve at validation.
106 malformed emails (4.7%) against a required contact.email field means roughly that many contacts will be rejected unless Apex supplies corrections.

`last_touch` has 8 future dates (up to 2027-08-05) and only 16.6% ISO-formatted values across six formats; if the customer chooses to use it for the rule 2 dormancy calculation, parse with an explicit format list and note that %m/%d/%y vs %d-%b-%Y ambiguity and the future dates will skew dormancy for those rows.
Rule 13 as written never produces the catalog's 'executive' role value; confirm with the customer (see the contact_role question) before the enum table is frozen.
subscriptions.json: 903 distinct acct_num values over 1003 rows means roughly 100 accounts hold more than one subscription. Confirm Meridian/the customer expects multiple subscription records per organization; if only one is wanted per account, a selection rule (e.g. latest start_date, or active over cancelled) is needed and that is a business decision for the engineer to raise.

Rule 11 ('trial subscriptions older than 90 days are dead and should not be migrated') needs a scope and a reference date before any records are dropped: 'trial' could mean the 27 rows with subscription_level = 'Trial' or the 84 rows with sub_status = 'trialing' (the two counts disagree, so they are not the same population), and '90 days' presumably counts from start_dt relative to the migration cutoff date. Agree both points before filtering, and note that 9 rows have a null start_dt so their age cannot be computed.

Rule 4 ('Strategic accounts always carry an Enterprise subscription; if billing shows something else, billing is wrong') requires joining to the accounts dataset on acct_num. The subscription file alone cannot apply it; expect plan overrides on Strategic accounts and expect those rows to differ from the source values.

Rule 7 depends on seat_count, but 41 rows (4.1%) have no seat count. Any 'Legacy Gold' row with a missing seat count cannot be resolved to enterprise vs professional by rule alone; flag these for the validation step.
subscription.seats, start_date and renewal_date are required in the target but the source has 41, 9 and 16 nulls respectively; defaults or rejection for those rows are a validation-step decision.
renew_dt has 80 future-dated values, which is expected for active subscriptions, but start_dt has 2 future dates (max 2027-08-01) which look like data entry errors worth checking during validation.

Target cross-record rule 'an inactive or churned organization cannot hold a trial or active subscription' can collide with customer rule 2 (dormant accounts forced to Inactive) and rule 6 (On Hold accounts stay active): any subscription here that maps to status active or trial under an account forced to Inactive will be rejected. Reconcile the account-side status mapping with these 548+ active/trialing subscriptions before load.
sub_status has case variants ('active' vs 'Active') and spelling variants ('canceled' vs 'cancelled', 'past due' vs 'past_due'); the mapping table above normalizes all of them, no data is lost.
activity.csv: acct_num must resolve to an organization that already exists (cross-record rule: an organization must exist before any activity references it). Confirm the 1000 distinct bare-numeric values are written in exactly the same form as organization.organization_id in the accounts dataset; if the account load prefixes or pads the id, the same rule must be applied here or every activity row will fail the reference check.

occurred_at has a stated range ending 2026-09-11, i.e. future-dated rows relative to a present-day migration. These may be scheduled or mis-keyed records; they also affect customer rule 2 (accounts with no activity in the last 18 months are dormant and become Inactive), since a future-dated activity would keep an otherwise dormant account looking active. Agree with the engineer on the reference date and whether future-dated activity counts before the dormancy derivation is run.

This dataset is the input to customer rule 2: the per-account max(occurred_at) over these 4947 rows drives the dormant -> organization.lifecycle_status = inactive decision on the account dataset. Derive it after the date normalization above, not from the raw strings.

amount is null or placeholder in 61.3% + 650 rows; this is expected for login, note and ticket kinds and should not be treated as a data defect. No default should be invented - activity.amount_usd is nullable.
activity_type has one case-variant group (Invoice / INVOICE); case folding is part of the enum mapping and does not need a customer decision.
Keys are clean: activity_id is 100% unique with no nulls and no exact duplicate rows, so idempotent re-sends are safe.

rows.reason: The catalog states the customer's legacy account number usually lands in organization.organization_id, and acct_num is the declared key column with 5-digit numeric values that satisfy the target pattern.
Exact name and meaning match with organization.name, the required display name of the account; values are company names up to 34 chars.

The values are account lifecycle states (Active/Inactive/Prospect/Churned) which line up with organization.lifecycle_status; subscription.status is the wrong home because 6 of 9 values have no meaning there and this file is the organization file.
The short codes are industry classifications and map one-to-one onto the organization.industry enum; only the two numeric codes are not self-evident.

organization.billing_region is the only state/province field in the catalog ('state or province code, e.g. CA, TX, ON') and hq_state holds US state and Canadian province values such as 'AB', 'GA', 'Colorado'.
organization.billing_country is the only country field and requires ISO 3166-1 alpha-2; the source holds the same concept in mixed notations.
Exact name and type match with organization.website (nullable URI).

organization.customer_since ('when the relationship started, per the customer's records') is the only date field on the organization entity, and the CRM account creation date is the closest available proxy; no other target fits.

account_priority is the only organization enum that can hold a 'strategic' designation and the catalog says it is explicitly not the plan; but Gold/Silver/Bronze are spend bands (rule 3) and the enum has only standard/priority/strategic, so collapsing them is a business decision.
Name and meaning match organization.annual_revenue_usd; values are revenue amounts, currently written as formatted text.
Exact name match with organization.employee_count (nullable integer); values are headcounts in the 22-3999 range.

There is no email field on the organization entity, and customer rule 1 states the account-row primary_contact_email is authoritative for creating or flagging the organization's primary contact, so it belongs on contact.email of a contact record keyed to this account.

These are internal Apex sales-rep person names (993 distinct, 'First Last' shapes), not customer data; the target catalog has no account-owner or user field, and contact.* is for customer-side contacts so mapping them there would create fake customer contacts.

The organization entity has no last-activity field; the only possible home is activity.occurred_at, which would mean fabricating one activity record per account (with an invented activity_id and kind). Whether to do that, or to use the date only to compute rule 2 dormancy and then drop it, is a business decision.

Only 4 distinct short values across 55% of rows, so this behaves like a coded flag rather than free text; it could become organization.tags (list of labels) or an activity of kind 'note' (activity.description), and which one is correct depends on what the four values mean to the business.
Unique, never null, 2279 distinct values shaped CT-000102 which already satisfy the contact_id pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$; it is the declared key of a contact dataset.

A 5-digit account number repeated across contacts (1046 distinct over 2279 rows) is the foreign key to the account; the catalog says the customer's legacy account number lands in organization.organization_id, so on a contact row it belongs in contact.organization_id.

The target has no single full-name field; contact.first_name and contact.last_name are both required, so this one column must be split across them. Mapped to first_name here because the schema allows one target per row; the same rule also populates contact.last_name.
Email-typed column on the contact row, name matches contact.email after synonyms, and contact.email is required.
Phone-typed column on the contact row; contact.phone is the only phone target and it is optional and nullable, which fits the 4.4% nulls.

The destination field is clearly contact.role, but rule 13 only covers 9 of the 12 observed values and it routes CEO/CTO to primary/technical, which leaves the catalog's 'executive' enum value unused; a business decision is needed on the remaining vocabulary before the mapping table is final.
Exact name and meaning match with contact.is_primary; the eight spellings are all yes/no tokens.

The contact entity has no last-contacted or date field at all. The only date-bearing targets are activity.occurred_at (which would mean synthesizing an activity record per contact) and organization.customer_since (a different concept), so a person must decide whether this column is carried over or dropped.

Meridian's contact entity has no marketing-preference or opt-out field, and rule 14 only requires that opted-out contacts still be migrated (214 'Y' rows) — it does not require the flag itself to be carried. There is therefore nothing to decide per field: the column is dropped and no contact is excluded because of it.
Name and meaning agree: a unique, non-null identifier (1003 distinct, 0 duplicates) in the form SUB-00415, which satisfies the target pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$ as-is.

This is the account the subscription belongs to; the catalog says the customer's legacy account number lands in organization.organization_id, so on a subscription row it is the foreign key subscription.organization_id. 903 distinct values over 1003 rows is consistent with accounts holding more than one subscription.

The values are plan names and the only plan enum in the catalog is subscription.plan (starter/professional/enterprise); customer rules 7 and 8 give an explicit translation table for most values. 'Trial' has no counterpart in the plan enum, so one value still needs a business decision.
Direct meaning match with subscription.billing_cycle; all six observed values collapse into the enum monthly/annual using the customer's rule 9 for the quarterly case.

Subscription lifecycle values map onto subscription.status (trial/active/past_due/cancelled); the alternative candidate organization.lifecycle_status is an account-level field and 7 of 9 values do not fit it. Rule 10 covers the two values the enum lacks.
Clear meaning match with the required integer field subscription.seats; the export types it inconsistently (709 int, 253 str) so a cast is needed.
Name and meaning agree with the required subscription.start_date; only 18.7% of values are already ISO 8601, so the six observed formats must be normalized.
Name and meaning agree with subscription.renewal_date; same six mixed date formats, only 18.2% ISO.

The only monetary field on the subscription entity is mrr_usd (monthly recurring revenue in USD), and rule 12 states the export's amounts are already monthly regardless of billing frequency, so the values land here directly without annual/monthly conversion.

The subscription entity has no currency field, and rule 12 explicitly says CAD amounts migrate as-is into USD, which makes the column redundant for the target model; the 75 CAD rows are already handled by the mrr_usd rule.
Exact name match to the activity primary key; 100% unique, no nulls, and the shape ACT-0003710 satisfies the catalog pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$ as-is.

1000 distinct values over 4947 rows with no nulls is the classic foreign key to the account; the catalog says the customer's legacy account number lands in organization.organization_id, so on an activity row it is the reference activity.organization_id. Numeric values like 10751 satisfy the id pattern.

Name and meaning match activity.kind; six of the eight observed values map cleanly to the enum after case folding, but 'Ticket' (618 rows) and 'Call' (215 rows) are not covered by the enum or by the customer's rules, so the vocabulary needs confirmation.
Exact name match to the required activity timestamp, no nulls, values are real datetimes; only the encoding differs across four formats.

Only monetary field on the activity row and the catalog's only activity amount; activity.amount_usd is nullable, which fits the 61.3% nulls (login, note and ticket rows carry no amount). Values arrive as mixed numeric text with symbols/separators and placeholders.

The activity entity has no currency field, and the column carries a single value (USD, 2563 rows; the rest blank), so it adds nothing. Customer rule 12 also says amounts migrate into the USD field as-is without conversion, which makes the column redundant rather than a decision for a person.
Exact name match to the optional, nullable activity.description; max length 24 and only six distinct short strings fit a free-text target without change.
